situation:
You are the marketing director for KILNROW COFFEE ROASTERS, a specialty coffee roastery in its second year of business. The owner (judge) started the company two years ago, roasts small lots for cafés and weekend markets, and has about five months of the first round of funding left to spend.

The roastery's advantage is a slow-drum roast profile the head roaster developed over those two years and wrote down as a step-by-step process the company has never patented and has never shown to anyone outside the roasting room. It is the reason three boutique hotels downtown pour KILNROW coffee in their lobbies.

WESTMARCH HOTELS, a forty-property chain, has offered a private-label supply agreement with guaranteed volume and cash paid quarterly in advance, enough to carry the roastery past the day the funding runs out. The agreement requires handing over the written roast profile so the chain can put its own name on every bag, which takes the KILNROW name off the cups and ends the head roaster's claim to the process the head roaster built.

The other course keeps the roast profile inside the roasting room and spends what is left of the funding on selling branded in-room coffee to boutique hotels one property at a time. Guest surveys the roastery ran last spring show travelers choose lodging coffee by the hotel's name and not the roaster's, against the head roaster's long experience that the label on the bag is what brings buyers back. That route may close no hotel before the money is gone.

The owner (judge) wants your analysis of what each course of action would do to the way the roastery promotes itself to hotels, and a recommendation on which one to take. The owner (judge) will greet you, ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the owner (judge) of KILNROW COFFEE ROASTERS. Business background is the same as the situation above.

You started the roastery two years ago and you are five months from the end of your first round of funding. You want to hear which course the marketing director recommends — the WESTMARCH HOTELS private-label supply agreement or selling branded in-room coffee under the roastery's own name — and you want to hear how the decision would be explained to the head roaster, who built the roast profile.

During the presentation you will ask the following questions:
judgeQuestions: How would you tell the head roaster what we have decided?
What would you say if the head roaster asked to keep the profile in our own name?
